title: Signature Dashed-Wave Running Stitch
description: Signature-original design: the even running stitch is re-spaced into a gentle wave, with stitch lengths rising and falling across the row, so the dashed line itself becomes a decorative wave. This is an original Signature design, not a traditional pattern.
materials: Thread to match or contrast the fabric
gauge: Aim for 4 to 6 stitches per inch for a visible basting or gathering line; 6 to 8 per inch for a finer seam. Keep every stitch the same length and every gap the same width so the dashed line reads evenly.
instructions: Mark a straight baseline and a light wave guide above it, then thread the needle with contrasting thread.
Work running stitches whose lengths grow from short to long and back to short across each wave, following the wave guide.
Keep the gaps between stitches equal while the stitch lengths change, so the wave reads clearly.
Repeat the wave across the row, then finish with a tiny backstitch on the back and trim.
stitch_chart: One row, worked left to right: up, down, up, down, in an even rhythm. Written as a repeat: [up 1 stitch-length, down 1 stitch-length] across the marked line. The chart reads as a dashed line: - - - - - - - -.
finished_uses: Basting seams before machine sewing, gathering fabric into ruffles, hand quilting through layers, simple mending, and decorative dashed outlines on embroidery.
variations: Work the design in a contrast thread to make the Signature shaping stand out.
Scale the repeat up or down by one stitch for finer or bolder versions of the same Signature design.
Combine the Signature design with its traditional counterpart in alternating bands for a sampler that shows both.

demo.code:
import sys

TITLE = 'Signature Dashed-Wave Running Stitch'
REPEAT = '- - '
WIDTH = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 24


def main():
    unit = len(REPEAT)
    reps = WIDTH // unit
    rem = WIDTH % unit
    row = (REPEAT * reps + REPEAT[:rem]).rstrip()
    print(TITLE + " - stitch-repeat planner")
    print("Width: %d stitches" % WIDTH)
    print("Repeat unit: %r (%d stitches)" % (REPEAT, unit))
    print("Repeats across: %d, remainder: %d" % (reps, rem))
    for r in range(1, 5):
        print("Row %d: %s" % (r, row))
    print("Total stitches in 4-row swatch: %d" % (WIDTH * 4))


main()
